papers.title: Covariate-Adaptive Studentized Sensitivity Analysis for Neyman’s Weak Null in Matched Designs
papers.source_caption: Matched sets. Each set: one treated unit and n_i − 1 controls.
papers.display_caption: Matched-set structure, from the CAWN presentation slides.
papers.alt: A matched-set schematic with I sets of varying sizes, each containing one treated unit and the remaining control units.
papers.summary: Develops covariate-adaptive sensitivity analysis for the sample-average treatment effect in matched observational studies. A closed-form lower-envelope statistic and studentization support asymptotically valid tests of Neyman’s weak null while allowing heterogeneous effects and unequal treatment probabilities within matched sets.
caveats: No manuscript figure was present in CAWeakNull (72).pdf; this image comes from the already public CAWN slides, not the manuscript.

papers.title: Stronger artificial intelligence breakthroughs hasten their own exhaustion
papers.display_caption: Cycles of idea creation and exhaustion following major AI breakthroughs.
papers.alt: Six panels show the idea life cycle, new and dead idea shares, AlexNet and Transformer citation patterns, successive active-idea cycles, and simulated effects of reciprocal reviewing.
papers.summary: Examines how major AI breakthroughs concentrate scientific attention and are followed by faster exhaustion of ideas. Analyses of publications and peer reviews, together with agent-based simulations, connect this pattern to declining diversity and the effects of reciprocal reviewing.
caveats: Use the user-confirmed Nature Machine Intelligence submission status, not the filename id or older Science submission.

papers.title: QEGF: A Quantum-Inspired Geometric and Energy-Based Fusion Framework for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
papers.source_caption: Overall architecture of the Quantum-Inspired Geometric and Energy-Based Fusion (QEGF) framework.
papers.display_caption: QEGF combines geometric multimodal fusion with energy-based uncertainty modeling.
papers.alt: QEGF architecture showing audio, text and video encoding, quantum-inspired geometric fusion, a task-adaptive transformer, energy-based uncertainty modeling, and uncertainty-guided prediction.
papers.summary: Combines geometric multimodal fusion with energy-based uncertainty modeling for sentiment analysis. Trace-normalized symmetric positive-definite descriptors model second-order correlations, while task-adaptive refinement and uncertainty estimates support robust predictions.
caveats: Quantum-inspired refers to geometric representations; this is not a quantum-computing implementation.
Figure extracted from the accepted author version; publisher headers were outside the natural figure bounds.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Graph Pooling Benchmark: Effectiveness, Robustness and Generalizability
papers.source_caption: Overview of our hierarchical backbone for graph classification and graph regression.
papers.display_caption: Shared hierarchical backbone used in the graph-pooling benchmark.
papers.alt: Graph-pooling benchmark backbone: message passing transforms the input graph, pooling reduces it, and readout produces a graph-level feature for supervised prediction.
papers.summary: Benchmarks 17 graph pooling methods across 28 datasets under shared experimental settings. Evaluates effectiveness, robustness to perturbations and distribution shifts, generalizability, and computational efficiency.
caveats: The source page has a For Peer Review watermark below the figure; it does not intersect the natural figure crop. No watermark was erased or modified.
This diagram illustrates the benchmark backbone, not a newly proposed pooling method.

papers.title: PVI-DPO: Perceptual Video Inpainting via Informative-Safe Preference Mining and Region-Aware Direct Preference Optimization
papers.source_caption: Single-frame background-restoration comparisons. Columns show the masked input, the compared method, and PVI-DPO; rows compare FloED and VideoPainter. Boxes highlight boundary discontinuities and structural artifacts, which are reduced by PVI-DPO.
papers.display_caption: Background-restoration comparisons against FloED and VideoPainter.
papers.alt: Two rows of video-inpainting comparisons show a bus and a mountain scene, with masked inputs, baseline reconstructions, and PVI-DPO results; boxes mark boundaries and structural details.
papers.summary: Learns video-inpainting preferences by contrasting ground-truth clips with carefully selected model failures localized to the masked region. A region-aware, winner-safe DPO objective emphasizes masked regions and boundaries while protecting the preferred reconstruction.
caveats: Uses the original qualitative comparison and original annotation boxes.
Figure 2 had a problematic black background in the PDF rendering; Figure 1 was selected for a faithful, readable image.
